actual_vote.A_tradeoffs: Alternative A (A_EXPLICIT_COMPLETE_RECORD) exposes the complete versioned RecoveryCheckpoint (moriarty-recovery-checkpoint/1) as a first-class value carrier across load_pair, inspect_pair, start, reopen, resume, recover, checkpoint_bytes, outcome_report, and reopen_report. Strengths: (1) Direct architectural alignment with existing mori_core::stage (B23/B26), which uses value-oriented transition functions rather than mutable stateful objects; (2) Zero impedance mismatch with the mandatory fresh-OS-process CLI and mori test lifecycle (B08), where every operation reads actual on-disk bytes, executes at most one transition, publishes a complete checkpoint file, and exits; (3) Complete boundary transparency—pending (with full unchanged Core2 Continuation), forward-complete (with final Snapshot), and recovery-complete (with site, await_label, handler, mode, and final Snapshot) control states, cumulative accounting (committed C, attempted_total T, committed_cap, ordered_effects), positive residual duties, and full ordered invocation history (Invocation[]) are directly inspectable without hidden VM caches or object state; (4) Clean failure immutability—consuming ReopenedRecovery by value and returning Result<RecoveryTransition, RecoveryFailure> avoids leaving an in-memory mutable object in an ambiguous partially mutated state on failure; (5) Distinct outcome_report(&RecoveryTransition) and reopen_report(&ReopenedRecovery) signatures cleanly separate state-changing transitions from event-free reopen (attempted=0, invocation=null). Costs/tradeoffs: (1) Explicit data duplication in serialized checkpoints (cumulative ordered_effects, full history with per-step snapshots, and current boundary/continuation), which requires explicit owner resource/size envelopes (O-TRACE, O-DURABLE, O-IO) rather than silent history truncation; (2) Library callers pass program and ReopenedRecovery explicitly rather than calling methods on a bundled process handle.
actual_vote.B_tradeoffs: Alternative B (B_OWNED_PROCESS_SAME_DURABLE_WIRE) wraps state in an owned RecoveryProcess with start/reopen constructors and resume(&mut self), recover(&mut self), checkpoint(&self), and report(&self) methods while requiring the exact same durable wire and fresh-process public CLI/test lifecycle. Strengths: (1) Bundles RecoveryProgram and current state into a single owned in-memory handle, which can prevent passing a mismatched program reference during multi-step in-memory library sequences; (2) Can encapsulate internal runtime caches if needed later. Costs/tradeoffs: (1) Redundant object lifecycle overhead on the mandatory public path—because every CLI command and mori test operation must execute in a fresh OS process over actual files (and cannot keep a RecoveryProcess alive across test steps), RecoveryProcess is reconstructed from bytes, mutated at most once, serialized, and dropped on every operation; (2) Ambiguous failure-mutation semantics on &mut self—mutating self in resume(&mut self)/recover(&mut self) requires an additional owner contract (api_alternative_B.failure_mutation_policy) to define whether self is rolled back, poisoned, or partially mutated when a transition fails; (3) Report state ambiguity—a single report(&self) method on RecoveryProcess must track hidden transient state to know whether the instance was just created via reopen (which requires operation="reopen", attempted="0", invocation=null) or just completed start/resume/recover; (4) Higher risk of encouraging in-memory test shortcuts (similar to stage_test.rs keeping Continuation in memory) instead of enforcing fresh-process file reopen. B can remain an optional internal refactor after adoption, but is inferior to A as the public contract.
actual_vote.reasoning: Independent evaluation of the 44 mandatory bodies (B01-B44) shows that Alternative A (A_EXPLICIT_COMPLETE_RECORD) is the cleaner, more direct, and more faithful ordinary architecture for Moriarty's paired durable-recovery companion (moriarty-recovery/1, moriarty-core2-recovery/1). Existing Core2 staged execution (B23 source/crates/mori-core/src/stage/admit.rs, B26 mod.rs) is structured around pure value-passing transitions (stage::load, stage::start, stage::resume) and explicit data carriers. Alternative A extends this discipline to paired recovery without mutating existing moriarty/2 Program, StagePlan, Continuation, StageEvent, or StageOutcome wire formats: handlers use a separate fresh-occurrence expression arena (guard root followed by left-to-right postorder body expressions) that never renumbers base ExprIds or await sites; the versioned RecoveryCheckpoint explicitly carries bindings, action, three normal control variants (pending, forward-complete, recovery-complete), cumulative accounting (committed C, attempted_total T, committed_cap, ordered_effects), positive residual duties, and complete Invocation[] history; and the public lifecycle connects real CLI bounded readers, language transitions, checkpoint publication, fresh-process event-free reopen, and fresh-process mori test execution. Alternative B adds mutable &mut self failure-state ambiguity and transient report-mode bookkeeping without reducing any wire, admission, or fresh-process persistence obligation. No blocking ordinary design defects were found; all 12 designated-owner security/admission/identity/ceiling/failure/IO prerequisites remain explicitly open and mandatory before dependent implementation.
